caption: The five-year survival rate for oral cancer caught early is 84%. When it's found late, that number drops to 38%. Those two bars represent the same disease, caught at different moments. The difference is often just knowing what to look for. A self-exam takes about two minutes. You're checking for white or red patches inside your mouth, sores that haven't healed in two weeks, any lumps along your jaw or neck, and any new difficulty swallowing. None of those things are easy to miss once you know to look. The habit is the hard part, and the habit is free. Run through your first check at oralcheck.org.
